source.title: Deep Learning on a Data Diet: Finding Important Examples Early in Training
source.authors: Mansheej Paul; S. Ganguli; G. Dziugaite

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It notes that this version corrects erroneous GraNd-at-initialization results caused by a Flax bug.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how pruning examples selected by GraNd or EL2N changes test accuracy, but it does not test the claim versions' specified interventions or measurements. In particular, it does not remove examples selected by memorization value or measure the training–test gap against magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: The paper's own pruning results and label-noise comparisons are recorded under fits_no_version. Claims about prior work, including memorization-based removal, are not recorded as this study's results. Values shown only in plots are kept as figure-only because the text does not give exact accuracies.
record.test_reason: The study measures generalization after EL2N/GraNd-based data selection, not removal based on memorization value as V8 specifies. Appendix G compares EL2N scores with supplied memorization values but does not test memorization-based removal. Its loss-landscape measurements do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization gaps. No other version's comparison is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: averaging early-training scores identifies subsets that preserve test accuracy, and excluding the highest-scoring examples can help depending on label noise and pruning level. These findings concern EL2N/GraNd scores, not inclusion-based memorization values.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses early-training example scoring and data pruning, rather than the interventions or measurements specified in the claim versions. Training uses SGD with momentum and weight decay; datasets are standard vision benchmarks with stated augmentation.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning fraction and score-window position change test accuracy; the effect of excluding the highest-scoring examples is stronger with 10% label randomization and is not observed in the clean-label 50%-subset condition. Averaging scores across initializations is reported as important for successful pruning.

fits_no_version.finding: Early EL2N-based pruning can preserve test accuracy while removing substantial fractions of training data; performance deteriorates at extreme pruning levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Averaged early-training example scores can identify subsets that preserve held-out accuracy in the tested vision settings.

fits_no_version.finding: At 40% retention, excluding the highest-EL2N-score examples improves performance in some windows, especially with label noise. At 50% retention with clean labels, the authors report no such boost. The record's statement that these examples reduce performance when excluded reverses the reported direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of excluding the highest-EL2N-score examples depends on label noise and the retained dataset fraction.

fits_no_version.finding: EL2N scores at epoch 20 do not appear correlated with supplied memorization values for 1,015 CIFAR-100 examples evaluated using ResNet50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early prediction-error scores and inclusion-based memorization values capture different aspects of example importance.

record.problems: Several relevant accuracy values are presented only in figures, without exact text values. Reported runs use four independent runs with variability shaded from the 16th to 84th percentile; the textual summary does not give uncertainty for the individual pruning claims. No claim-version intervention is directly tested.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version-matched results were reported. Other plotted score-sensitivity, architecture-transfer, and training-dynamics results concern the scoring method or related constructs, not the listed claim versions or the training–test gap measure they specify.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating training recipes.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing high-memorization-value examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions because their interventions match none. The corrected version explicitly rejects the earlier GraNd-at-initialization findings; the Discussion retains an inconsistent statement about successful pruning at initialization. Appendix G is already declared in the record, so it is not a missing claim-version result.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with generalization on natural labels under the specified architectures and recipes.
Does not sweep network width across the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks or test local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD for held-out performance.
Does not vary batch size or test large-batch generalization penalties.
Does not add or remove dropout or weight decay as the tested intervention.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove examples selected by memorization value and retrain against random-example removal; it only compares memorization values with EL2N scores.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Retrained on the highest-EL2N-score subset after pruning the lowest-scoring examples.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy versus training on the full dataset
rows.baseline: training on the full dataset; exact accuracy not stated
rows.value: can prune 50% of examples without affecting accuracy
rows.uncertainty: not stated for this textual result
rows.note: The paper reports this as a general finding; the plotted values are not stated numerically in the text.
rows.check: Valid data-pruning result, but no listed version measures this intervention. Its reported preservation of accuracy cannot establish a claim-version effect.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Retrained on the highest-EL2N-score subset after pruning the lowest-scoring examples.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy versus training on the full dataset
rows.baseline: training on the full dataset; exact accuracy not stated
rows.value: 25% of examples can be pruned with only a 1% drop in accuracy
rows.uncertainty: not stated for this textual result
rows.note: The stated result is a small test-accuracy loss after pruning.
rows.check: No listed version matches this intervention. The introduction reports a 1% accuracy drop, but Contributions reports no loss for EL2N pruning of 25% of CIFAR-100; the row should acknowledge this inconsistency rather than assign the introductory result unambiguously to EL2N.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a sliding window of examples ranked by EL2N score.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy as the score window moves to higher percentiles
rows.baseline: full-data and random-pruning baselines are plotted; exact values not stated
rows.value: performance increases as the window moves higher, except when it includes examples with the very highest scores; the optimal window excludes approximately 500 highest-scoring training examples
rows.note: The paper describes the direction and approximate number of excluded examples, not exact accuracy values.
rows.check: The sliding-window result does not test memorization-based removal. Excluding the approximately 500 highest-scoring examples improves accuracy relative to retaining the highest-score window in this fixed-size subset experiment.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a sliding window of examples ranked by EL2N score.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy as the score window moves to higher percentiles
rows.baseline: full-data and random-pruning baselines are plotted; exact values not stated
rows.value: with increased label corruption, the optimal window shifts and excludes a higher number of examples
rows.note: The paper states that the shift and exclusion effect increase with label corruption.
rows.check: No listed version matches the intervention. Appendix B.3 specifies permuting labels among a randomly selected 10% of examples, preserving label counts; this is not a fully random-label fitting experiment.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained after discarding the highest-scoring examples from a 50% subset.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy as the score offset changes
rows.baseline: full-data and random-pruning baselines are plotted; exact values not stated
rows.value: no longer see a boost in performance from dropping the highest score examples; decreasing marginal gains
rows.note: The paper explicitly says the clean-label boost seen at the higher pruning level is absent in this lower-pruning regime.
rows.check: The reported absence concerns an accuracy boost from excluding the highest EL2N scores, not absence of any listed claim effect. The operation is a sliding window retaining 50% of the original dataset, replacing examples as the window moves.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained after discarding the highest-scoring examples from a 50% subset.
rows.measure: Final test accuracy as the score offset changes
rows.baseline: full-data and random-pruning baselines are plotted; exact values not stated
rows.note: The text's explicit qualification concerns the no-randomized-label condition; it does not state the corresponding noisy-label result.
rows.check: No listed version matches this intervention, and the supplied figure text does not establish the accuracy trend. As in R5, the experiment retains a sliding 50% window rather than simply discarding examples from a preselected subset.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
